bib.title: GANs Trained by a Two Time-Scale Update Rule Converge to a Local Nash Equilibrium

read.skipped: Appendix A2/A3 convergence proofs (math) only skimmed by heading; main text, FID appendix, experiments appendix, A5, A6 read in full

question: Can GANs be proven to converge to a local Nash equilibrium with separate discriminator and generator learning rates, and does this improve training and how should image GANs be evaluated?
hypothesis: A two time-scale update rule (discriminator learns faster in theory) stabilises GAN training and yields better FID than equal learning rates.
contributions: The two time-scale update rule for GANs
Proof that GANs trained with TTUR converge to a stationary local Nash equilibrium
Description of Adam as heavy ball with friction and its second order differential equation
Convergence of GANs trained with TTUR and Adam
The Frechet Inception Distance (FID), more consistent than the Inception Score

method.summary: Separate learning rates b (discriminator) and a (generator) are used with Adam on DCGAN, WGAN-GP (image and char-level language) and BEGAN, compared against equal-rate training; evaluation uses the newly introduced FID (images) or JSD (text).
method.task: image and text generation with GANs; GAN evaluation

models.name: DCGAN
models.architecture: deep convolutional GAN, carpedm20 TF implementation

models.name: WGAN-GP language (gan_language.py)
models.architecture: 1D CNN generator and 1D CNN discriminator over one-hot 32-char sequences

models.name: Inception-v3 (pretrained, inception-2015-12-05)
models.architecture: CNN; last pooling layer used as coding layer for FID

training.objective: Original GAN loss (DCGAN), Wasserstein with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP), BEGAN
training.lr: per experiment (b discriminator, a generator): DCGAN CelebA 1e-5/5e-4, CIFAR-10 1e-4/5e-4, SVHN 1e-5/1e-4, LSUN 1e-5/1e-4; WGAN-GP image and language 3e-4/1e-4; orig equal rates 1e-4 to 5e-4
training.steps: stopped when FID/JSD no longer decreasing; best at e.g. 225k (CelebA DCGAN), 168k iter (WGAN-GP CIFAR-10)
training.regularisation: weight decay suggested in theory (A4, A5), not reported in experiments
training.wall_clock: WGAN-GP: 700 to 2010 min per run to best point
training.seeds: 8 runs (image), 10 runs (language) per learning-rate setting; fixed random seeds removed from reference code

other.orig WGAN-GP critic steps: 5 (image) and 10 (language) per generator step; TTUR uses 1
other.learning rates: chosen as large as possible while FID or JSD keeps decreasing
other.FID evaluation frequency: every 1,000 DCGAN mini-batches, every 5,000 WGAN-GP outer iterations (images), every 100 (language)

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet distance between Gaussians fitted to Inception-v3 pool features of real and generated images: ||m-mw||^2 + Tr(C+Cw-2(C Cw)^1/2)

metrics.name: normalized JSD
metrics.definition: Jensen-Shannon divergence between model and real n-gram statistics (4-gram, 6-gram)

baselines: Same GAN with one time-scale (equal learning rates), 'orig'
eval.protocol: Mean, min and max over 8 (images) or 10 (language) runs per setting; best FID at tuned number of updates; no significance test

evidence.quote: For TTUR however, the discriminator is updated only once per iteration.

results.claim: TTUR gives lower FID than one time-scale training for DCGAN on CelebA (12.5 vs 21.4).
results.setup: DCGAN, CelebA, TTUR b=1e-5 a=5e-4 at 225k updates vs orig 5e-4 at 70k; best over updates; 8 runs per setting
results.table: Table 1, DCGAN CelebA, TTUR vs orig, column FID

results.claim: TTUR improves WGAN-GP FID on LSUN Bedrooms from 20.5 to 9.5.
results.setup: WGAN-GP image model, LSUN Bedrooms, TTUR b=3e-4 a=1e-4, 1900 min vs orig 1e-4, 2010 min
results.table: Table 1, WGAN-GP Image LSUN, column FID

results.claim: TTUR improves WGAN-GP FID on CIFAR-10 from 29.3 to 24.8.
results.setup: WGAN-GP image, CIFAR-10, TTUR 3e-4/1e-4 at 700 min (168k iter) vs orig 1e-4 at 800 min (53k iter)
results.table: Table 1, WGAN-GP Image CIFAR-10, column FID

results.claim: TTUR improves DCGAN FID on LSUN Bedrooms from 70.4 to 57.5.
results.setup: DCGAN, LSUN Bedrooms, TTUR 1e-5/1e-4 at 340k vs orig 5e-5 at 70k

results.claim: On DCGAN CIFAR-10 TTUR gains only 0.8 FID (36.9 vs 37.7).
results.setup: DCGAN, CIFAR-10, TTUR 1e-4/5e-4 at 75k vs orig 1e-4 at 100k

results.claim: On the One Billion Word benchmark TTUR lowers normalized JSD slightly: 4-gram 0.35 vs 0.38, 6-gram 0.74 vs 0.77.
results.setup: WGAN-GP char-level language model, TTUR 3e-4/1e-4, 10 runs

results.claim: FID is computed from 50,000 generated images through Inception-v3 pool layer and Gaussian Frechet distance.
results.quote: To approximate these moments for the model distribution, we generate 50,000 images, propagate them through the Inception-v3 model, and then compute the mean m and the covariance matrix C.

results.claim: FID increases monotonically with disturbance level while Inception Score fluctuates, stays flat or decreases.
results.setup: CelebA with six disturbance types (noise, blur, rectangles, swirl, salt and pepper, ImageNet contamination)
results.quote: The FID captures the disturbance level very well by monotonically increasing whereas the Inception Score ﬂuctuates,

results.claim: TTUR with Adam converges to a stationary local Nash equilibrium under assumptions A1-A5 (Borkar 1997); Adam follows a heavy ball with friction ODE.
results.setup: Theory; requires Lipschitz gradients (not ReLU), a(n)=o(b(n)), stationary second moments for Adam
results.quote: Theorem 2. If Adam is used with β1 = 1 −a(n + 1)r(n), β2 = 1 −αa(n + 1)r(n)

results.claim: TTUR gives no gain for BEGAN since its equilibrium term ties the two gradients.
results.setup: BEGAN on CelebA and LSUN Bedrooms, 8 runs
results.quote: For BEGAN we cannot ensure TTUR by adjusting learning rates.

limits: Convergence proof needs Lipschitz gradients (excludes ReLU) and stationary second moments of the gradient for Adam.
Learning rates must be found per experiment; best-over-training FID reported without significance tests.
TTUR gives no gain for BEGAN.
Theory suggests discriminator faster, yet DCGAN uses larger generator rate; authors argue not contradictory (A5).
FID assumes Gaussian Inception features and uses ImageNet Inception-v3.
Dataset sizes, batch sizes and architectures not stated in the paper.

terms.definition: Frechet distance between Gaussians (mean, covariance) fitted to Inception coding-layer activations of real and generated images
two time-scale update rule: individual learning rate for discriminator and generator
